context: Define the durable job contract and lifecycle before implementation, including tenant ownership, idempotency, terminal states, cancellation races, retries, leases, artifact publication, retention, and crash recovery. Reuse existing benchmark execution and result-bundle creation behind a worker boundary. Return explicit execution_id handles immediately, persist state transitions and ownership transactionally, and make status/result/cancel safe on any worker. Preserve the synchronous run_benchmark tool for compatible local clients until a separately reviewed deprecation decision.
description: Current MCP benchmark execution is synchronous even though results already have explicit execution IDs and files. For remote multi-user and horizontally scaled operation, long-running runs need durable application state that survives worker changes, deploys, retries, and cancellation. Introduce start_benchmark, get_benchmark_status, get_benchmark_result, and cancel_benchmark around a shared job store and queue. Do not turn the currently unused process-global ExecutionTracker into the authoritative HTTP state store.

anti_patterns.dont: activate benchbox.mcp.execution.ExecutionTracker as the HTTP job store
anti_patterns.instead: use a durable shared repository and queue
anti_patterns.why: process-global memory is lost across workers, restarts, and deploys

anti_patterns.dont: hold an MCP request open for the full remote benchmark run
anti_patterns.instead: return an execution_id and expose explicit status/result/cancel tools
anti_patterns.why: long requests are fragile across proxies, clients, and deployments

anti_patterns.dont: infer job ownership from an MCP protocol session
anti_patterns.instead: persist authenticated principal ownership with the job
anti_patterns.why: modern MCP requests are sessionless and can hit any worker

preserves.behavior: A completed result is published atomically and never reported complete before its artifact is durable
Every job and artifact is bound to the authenticated principal/workspace and inaccessible across tenants
Existing benchmark execution semantics and exported result-bundle format remain unchanged
Existing synchronous run_benchmark remains available for compatible local clients until separately deprecated

prior_art.concept: existing synchronous benchmark execution and execution_id creation
existing result discovery by filename and execution ID

work_units.summary: Specify the durable job state machine, ownership model, idempotency, leases, cancellation, retries, retention, and recovery semantics
Implement a shared job repository and bounded queue with transactional state transitions
Extract existing benchmark execution behind a worker boundary that publishes result bundles atomically
Add tenant-scoped start_benchmark, get_benchmark_status, get_benchmark_result, and cancel_benchmark tools
Handle duplicate submission, worker loss, lease expiry, cancellation races, retries, and orphaned artifacts
Add two-worker and restart recovery tests plus compatibility coverage for synchronous run_benchmark
